Validation record

  • PR #22: 150 offline/loopback tests passed, one skipped; encoder gate checks passed.
  • Migration: identity, missing-card, stale-token, busy-stop, experimental-opt-in, stopped-owner status, lifecycle discovery and rootless routing fixture checks added.
  • All three model files transferred to XFS and passed SHA256 verification; the pinned ROCm image imported into the dedicated Podman store.
  • Live Qwen 64k inference and OpenCode passed as recorded below. Other profiles, live MCP lifecycle and physical boot checks remain pending.
  • Physical cold boots with and without the eGPU have not yet been tested for this configuration.

Live Radeon / OpenCode smoke check

The laptop runs OpenCode 2.0.31. Its private consumer key and generated provider configuration were installed from merged machine-setup main, and the running OpenCode service accepted opencode reload. Both its running model list and a standalone model list include 7900xt/7900xt and all retained concrete choices. A real opencode run --standalone --model 7900xt/7900xt returned RADEON_OK. The selected backend remains Qwen 64k so it is available for interactive use.

Check Observed
Compute enumeration Exactly AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT, 20464 MiB
VRAM allocated after warmup 16,202,002,432 bytes (15.09 GiB)
Authenticated request from bigcachy RADEON_OK, 0.326 seconds
Short request tokens 20 prompt / 5 generated
Short request generation rate 27.54 tokens/second
Backend / gateway Both active; enabled for user startup; linger enabled

These are functional smoke measurements, not a sustained throughput, large-context or concurrent-slot benchmark. Structured evidence.

Initial rootless startup exposed only the card's render node. ROCm failed to initialise and llama.cpp silently used CPU despite the proxy reporting ready. Giving ROCr /dev/dri for enumeration and setting ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-255c7a14946751e2 resolved this on the mixed-GPU laptop. Default seccomp remains enabled. The runtime now runs a compute-device probe before serving and refuses CPU/iGPU fallback or unexpected devices. Regression coverage checks those refusal cases. The internal 780M is not used for inference.

Radeon 128k-only configuration correction

Later on 2026-10-17 the Radeon Qwen 64k option was retired at the user's request. All retained Radeon models now provide 131072 tokens per slot. Earlier 64k results above are historical, not the current menu or saved selection.

The active backend was already running Qwen at 131072, but OpenCode's generic Radeon/Qwen entries still advertised 61440 tokens. This caused early compaction. All three development client configs now use 126976 tokens for those entries; supported configuration reloads succeeded without inference restarts. The user confirmed Bigcachy's active agent changed from 25k at 41% to 35k at 28%.

The sequential migration harness is preserved in benchmarks/oculink.py, updated to test only retained profiles. Run it explicitly on the owner during an agreed idle testing window; it switches profiles and restores the saved selection. It was not run during this correction because the user was actively coding.
